paragraphs.text: This is [Meizhan](yancha:meizhan), a Fujian cultivar that came from Anxi, made in 1990 as [Wuyi rock tea](yancha:definition) from the [Wuyi Mountains](wuyi-mountains:where-it-is). It is less famous than Rougui and Shui Xian and is not one of the four famous bushes of Wuyi. The leaf was twisted into long strips and given a heavy [charcoal roast](yancha:making) in the traditional rock tea way. That roast dries the leaf so it keeps.

A roast this heavy marks the kind of rock tea that is put away for years, because the heavier the roast, the longer the tea is said to stay good. Over thirty-six years the roast has settled fully into the leaf. Kept sealed, dry and cool, it is spared [going green again](yancha:ageing), the damp fault of stored rock tea.

brewing.text: Wuyi tea is usually brewed gongfu style with water at or near the boil, about 95 to 100°C, and about 5 to 8 grams of leaf in a 100 to 120 ml gaiwan, a third to a half full. A quick rinse, poured off at once, is common. Steeps start short, about 5 to 20 seconds, and grow a few seconds longer each round, and good rock tea gives seven steeps or more. In a larger pot, use about 2 to 5 grams for 250 to 350 ml and steep two to three minutes.

notice.text: A smoother, thicker liquor with less sharpness, the roast softened and the high aroma faded.
